newsitem.title: UK: Shell says could add 10-20 mln bls to Brent field.
newsitem.headline: Shell says could add 10-20 mln bls to Brent field.

text.p: Shell U.K. Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) said on Tuesday they had successfully tested a new technique to tap into small reservoirs which could add another 10-20 million barrels to reserves of the North Sea Brent field.

The company, which operates the Brent pipeline system, said in a statement that a well drilled using existing infrastructure in a small reservoir from the Brent Delta platform started flowing at the end of October and is currently producing 6,000 barrels per day.
The reservoir, with estimated reserves of 500,000 barrels of oil, had previously been considered uneconomic to develop, it added.
The technique used involves feeding slim line tubing from a coil down into an existing well. The cost of developing the well was around half the cost of a conventional well, Shell Expro said.

"Brent at present has estimated remaining recoverable reserves of more than 400 million barrels of oil. We estimate that by drilling a number of coiled tubing wells over the next few years we can tap into another 10 or 20 million barrels," Shell Expro said.
Shell Expro is a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp.

Brent system throughput includes crude produced from 13 fields and several satellite wells piped to Sullom Voe terminal in the Shetland Islands for blending with Ninian crude and exported as Brent Blend.

The Brent field is currently undergoing a major redevelopment programme costing a total of $1.3 billion. Current production from Brent Delta averages about 55,000 bpd. The field daily average is about 190,000 bpd, Shell Expro said.
